source: When a major port becomes congested, ships wait offshore, containers pile up, and trucking schedules slip. Retailers respond by ordering earlier and holding more inventory, which ties up cash and warehouse space. Delays at one port also push cargo to alternatives that were never built to absorb the extra volume, spreading the jam.
summary: Port congestion triggers offshore ship delays, container backups, and disrupted trucking schedules, prompting retailers to order early and stockpile inventory, straining cash flow and storage, while diverted cargo overwhelms unprepared alternative ports, worsening the issue.

source: Compound interest means earning returns on both the money you put in and the returns already earned. Over short periods the effect looks small, but over decades it dominates. This is why starting to save early matters more than saving a larger amount later, and why fees that look tiny each year can consume a large share of long-run gains.
summary: Compound interest is when you earn returns not just on your initial investment but also on the returns it generates. Over time, this snowball effect becomes increasingly powerful. Starting to save early beats saving larger amounts later because compounding has more time to work. Similarly, even small annual fees can significantly reduce your long-term gains due to compounding working against you. Save early, minimize fees, and let time do the heavy lifting!

source: Inflation reduces what a given amount of money can buy. If wages rise more slowly than prices, households feel poorer even though their paycheck is larger in nominal terms. Economists therefore compare real wages, which adjust for price changes, rather than nominal wages when judging whether living standards are improving.
summary: Inflation decreases the purchasing power of money, making households feel poorer if prices rise faster than wages. To assess living standards, economists focus on real wages, which account for price changes, rather than nominal wages.

source: Dense city centres are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, an effect known as the urban heat island. Dark roofs and pavement absorb sunlight, buildings block wind, and there are fewer plants to cool the air by evaporation. Planting trees, using lighter surfaces and adding green roofs can reduce the difference.
summary: Dense city centers experience higher temperatures than rural areas due to the **urban heat island (UHI) effect**, caused by dark, heat-absorbing surfaces (like roofs and pavement), reduced greenery, and blocked airflow from buildings. Mitigation strategies include planting trees, using reflective materials, and installing green roofs to cool the environment.

source: Observability for AI agents means recording every step a request takes: the prompt, each tool call, the model's reply, and the time and tokens each step used. With those traces, a team can replay a failed session, find the step that went wrong, and tell a slow tool from a slow model. Without them, a wrong answer is just a mystery.
summary: Observability for AI agents involves tracking every step of a request, including prompts, tool calls, model responses, and resource usage like time and tokens. This allows teams to replay failed sessions, identify errors or inefficiencies, and diagnose issues. Without such traces, wrong answers remain unexplained.

source: Remote work changed more than where people sit. Teams that once relied on hallway conversations had to write things down, and many discovered that clear written decisions made meetings shorter and onboarding faster. At the same time, managers found it harder to notice when someone was struggling, and newer employees missed the informal mentoring that happens when people share a room. Companies that did well tended to be explicit about which work needs real-time collaboration and which does not, to set norms for response times, and to bring people together in person for planning and relationship-building rather than for routine updates. Those that treated remote work as the old office with the video turned on often saw communication overhead grow without any of the flexibility benefits.
summary: Remote work transformed communication and collaboration, improving clarity and efficiency but introducing challenges like reduced mentoring and oversight, with success hinging on intentional practices and in-person relationship-building.

source: Technical debt describes the future cost of choosing a quick solution now. A shortcut can be the right call when a deadline is real, but the debt accrues interest: every later change takes longer because the code is harder to understand. Teams that track their debt and schedule time to repay it avoid a slowdown that otherwise arrives gradually and then all at once.
summary: Technical debt is the future cost of quick solutions, as it makes code harder to modify over time. Teams that track and address it proactively can prevent gradual, then sudden, slowdowns.
